payload.goal: An operator always knows whether a drive run is alive and how far it has got — in the calling session, on the status bar, and in the sofar apps — without asking an agent or opening another terminal, and one run can never be driven by two drivers at once. Liveness is decided by a machine-local lock the OS releases on exit, never by a heartbeat or a record event; a heartbeat exists only to show presence to remote viewers.

plan.goal: An operator always knows whether a drive run is alive and how far it has got — in the calling session, on the status bar, and in the sofar apps — without asking an agent or opening another terminal, and one run can never be driven by two drivers at once. tasks.title: docs/SPEC.md Driver section gains: run liveness (a machine-local exclusion held for the run's life and released by the OS on exit; a fresh start and --resume refuse while it is held), the status bar drive segment, `sofar drive --follow`, and the remote presence contract; acceptance entries. Log a Decision qualifying in-session-drive D2 (no pid in the record, no pid file beside it) BEFORE any code.

Rule on remote presence against the guard-rails before any code: a ping sent only when the repo is linked to sofar cloud, carrying run id, slug, task and state and no user content. Log a Decision on whether it is sync (client side allowed) or telemetry emission (a rail it would have to name), and state that the server half is built in sofar-cloud, not here.

Run lock: the driver holds it from taking the run until run_stopped; a new run and --resume refuse while it is held, naming the live driver's log; a crash or kill -9 releases it, sleep does not. Mechanism within the dependency law (node built-ins; flock would need a dependency and a Decision). Tests: two drivers on one run, kill -9 then resume, leftover artefact after a crash.

`sofar status` (one-shot and --watch) shows a run as running, driver gone (no run_stopped, lock free) or stopped wherever the lock is visible; `sofar drive --stop` against a gone driver says so at once instead of waiting 30s. Tests.

Status bar drive segment: when the session's initiative has a live run, show run state and the task in flight next to done/total; a gone or stopped run shows its reason; within the statusline laws (glyph vocabulary, color law, one line, 10s refreshInterval). rust-core 2.6 statusline parity must include it. Tests.

`sofar drive <slug> --follow`: prints one line per handoff, task status change and run warning; exits on run_stopped AND when the driver's lock is gone, so it can never stay silent over a crashed driver; plain line output usable as a Claude Code Monitor command. Tests.

Protocol block (CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md): after `sofar drive --detach`, the agent watches `sofar drive <slug> --follow` (Monitor where the host has it) and relays needs_user and stop events; hosts without a monitor are told to point the operator at the status bar or `sofar status`. Previous block kept as a shipped version.

Client side, per the 1.2 Decision: a linked repo's driver sends presence at start, on each handoff, on a fixed interval and at stop; nothing when unlinked; never a record event; failures to reach the API never affect the run. Tests with injected fetch.

Server contract handed to sofar-cloud: the TTL after which a driver reads as offline, and what the Mac, iPhone and web apps render for running, offline and stopped. Written here; built in sofar-cloud.

Proof from a live Claude Code session on a throwaway initiative: detach a run; status bar shows it within one refresh; Monitor notifications arrive per handoff; a second --resume while it lives is refused; kill -9 the driver, status shows driver gone, --follow exits, --resume is allowed. Record the numbers.
README + release staged for the user to publish.

payload.text:
RESEARCH (2026-09-17, four parallel agents + local checks) — what beats or changes the first plan.

1. LIVENESS. Keep an OS-released lock; change the mechanism from a listening unix socket to a FILE lock. Sockets fail where --detach is launched from: Claude Code's Linux sandbox seccomp blocks AF_UNIX (anthropics/claude-code#44180), macOS Seatbelt denies bind (#39257; measured EPERM under (deny network*)), kill -9 leaves a stale socket file whose cleanup races (VS Code claimInstance does unlink+retry), and the 104-byte path limit. File lock facts: Node has no lock API (nodejs/node#49256, #54446 closed); macOS O_EXLOCK (0x20)|O_NONBLOCK via fs.openSync works with zero deps — REPRODUCED locally on Node 24.15: busy (EAGAIN) while held and while SIGSTOPped, free after kill -9. Linux has no O_EXLOCK: portable zero-dep option is node:sqlite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE (unflagged since Node 22.13; engines floor is >=18 today) or a flock(1) child. Lock file lives in a per-user machine-local cache dir keyed by run id, never in the repo or an iCloud/Dropbox/SMB path; never unlinked. Rust side must use the SAME primitive (std File::try_lock is flock on Unix, stable since 1.89; if Node uses sqlite, Rust uses rusqlite on the same file). Rejected: pid/hostname-pid files (Bazel #12591, #11020), heartbeat locks (proper-lockfile), pidfd/kqueue exit watching (needs a pid), localhost TCP ports. ADD fencing: run_started is epoch 1, each --resume appends run_adopted {run, epoch:max+1}; a driver seeing a newer adoption in its pre-launch fold or 2s byte scan steps down without run_stopped; stop requests count by log order after the adoption instead of the wall-clock adoptedAt check. One durable fact per takeover, not a heartbeat; covers other machines/users/containers after sync (Kleppmann 2016-02-08; Kafka KIP-98 producer epochs).

2. PROGRESS IN SESSION. Monitor watches are capped at 30 min since Claude Code 2.1.271 (no persistent option; confirmed in this session's Monitor schema) and every notification is a model turn, so --follow under Monitor as the default either goes silent or bills idle turns. Replace with `sofar drive <slug> --await`: one-shot, exits with one line on needs_user, run_stopped or driver gone; the agent runs it with run_in_background (no deadline, zero tokens while waiting). Routine progress goes to zero-cost surfaces: statusline segment (refreshInterval redraws while idle; terminal CLI only — the Claude desktop app ignores statusLine, anthropics/claude-code#41456) and a UserPromptSubmit drive line only when something changed (~50 tokens, next prompt, never wakes). Prototype an asyncRewake PostToolUse hook on Bash(sofar drive *) (wakes an idle session via exit 2) — unverified that multi-hour hook timeouts hold. Codex hooks are stable and on in codex-cli 0.136.0 (verified locally) so Codex can be Tier 2 and SPEC Host tiers is stale. Keep --follow for terminals / opt-in narration. Check in proof: Claude Code stops setsid-detached processes when a background task or session ends. Still rejected: channels (research preview, allowlist), MCP push (2026-07-28 spec replaced resources/subscribe; no host puts updates in model context), posting to the messaging socket (peer-messaging D1).

3. APPS. Nothing replaces local file watch + sofar serve SSE + the doorbell. Mac app: Swift FSEvents on .sofar/initiatives/ (survives git rename) + UniFFI fold (UniFFI 0.32.1: async fns, foreign traits; wrap in AsyncStream); full fold measured 4.3 ms on a 1.09 MB log, so byte-offset folding is optional. GAP: nothing syncs during a run — pushStream is only called by manual `sofar push` (packages/engine/src/cli/cloud.ts:401), so iPhone/web see nothing mid-run; a linked driver must push (debounced) as it appends. Best lock-screen/menu-bar surface: iPhone Live Activity driven by APNs (push-to-start iOS 17.2; shows in the Mac menu bar on macOS 26+; Mac apps cannot create Live Activities; 4 KB payload; ended after 8 h so long runs restart it; a Live Activity cannot fetch, so task titles would transit APNs — needs a content ruling or counts-only). Plus MenuBarExtra in the Mac app and time-sensitive notifications for needs_user/stopped/driver gone. Rejected: LiveStore (total-order rebase clashes with ulid fold), Zero/Electric/PowerSync (Postgres row replication), Convex/InstantDB (hosted DB becomes truth), Automerge/Loro (CRDTs solve a problem the log does not have), WebSocket/WebTransport (no gain over SSE). Borrow from Durable Streams: catch-up then live data on the same SSE, saving a round trip per ring. New Rust crates need a Decision (rust-core D1 allows serde, serde_json, ulid).

4. REMOTE PRESENCE. Keep heartbeat + TTL; connection-based presence loses (driver holds no cloud connection; SSE cannot prove client liveness; half-open sockets hide a sleeping Mac for minutes; VS Code tunnels shows live machines offline). Server: one row per run, state computed at read (last_seen > now - ttl), no sweeper. Driver: ping every 30s ±10% jitter and immediately on start, handoff, wake and stop; 10s AbortSignal timeout; failed pings dropped, never queued; seq/boot nonce. Wake detection: local 5s tick, ping at once when wall clock jumps >2 ticks. TTL 90s (matches doorbell 25s/90s). UX: Running (task · Ns ago) / Not responding ("last seen 14:02 — asleep, offline or crashed", never "offline since") / Stopped (reason) / viewer's own feed stale. Never infer stopped from silence. Privacy: ids only (run, slug, task, state, seq, interval), device name from the existing token, linked repos only with opt-out, one overwritten row, deleted N days after stop, never analytics. Optional product choice: `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` keeps the Mac from idle sleep during a run (not lid close).

plan.goal: An operator always knows whether a drive run is alive and how far it has got — in the calling session, on the status bar, and in the sofar apps — without asking an agent or opening another terminal, and one run can never be driven by two drivers at once. Liveness is decided by a machine-local lock the OS releases on exit, never by a heartbeat or a record event; a heartbeat exists only to show presence to remote viewers.

tasks.title: Operator rulings, each logged as a Decision before dependent work: (a) lock primitive — raise engines to Node >=22.13 for node:sqlite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE on every OS, or per-platform (macOS O_EXLOCK, Linux flock child, Windows UV_FS_O_EXLOCK); (b) an empty OS-released lock file in a per-user cache dir is NOT the pid file in-session-drive D2 forbids; (c) presence ping is user-facing sync, not telemetry emission (ids only, linked repos, opt-out, one overwritten row); (d) task titles may transit APNs for Live Activities, or counts only; (e) whether a run keeps the Mac awake with caffeinate -i -w.

Prototype an asyncRewake PostToolUse hook on Bash(sofar drive *) that runs --await and wakes an idle Claude Code session; measure whether a multi-hour hook timeout holds. Keep it only if it does; log the result.

Protocol block (CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md): after --detach the agent starts `sofar drive <slug> --await` in its background shell (or relies on the 3.5 hook) and relays what it prints; hosts without a background shell point the operator at the prompt line, statusline or `sofar status`. plan.goal: An operator always knows whether a drive run is alive and how far it has got — in the calling session, on the status bar, and in the sofar apps — without asking an agent or opening another terminal, and one run can never be driven by two drivers at once. Liveness is decided by a machine-local lock the OS releases on exit, never by a heartbeat or a record event; a heartbeat exists only to show presence to remote viewers.

tasks.title: Operator rulings, each logged as a Decision before dependent work. Recommended in the 2026-09-17 session: (a) lock primitive = flock semantics everywhere — Rust std File::try_lock (zero crates under rust-core D1), Swift flock, Node O_EXLOCK on macOS (verified to contend with flock), Linux flock(1) child until sofar-core binaries ship; no Node floor raise, no node:sqlite/rusqlite; (b) an empty OS-released lock file under the per-user state dir is NOT the pid file in-session-drive D2 forbids (clarify D2, do not overturn); (c) the presence ping is user-facing sync for cloud-linked repos, not telemetry emission; (e) keep-awake lives in the engine as a ~/.config/sofar setting (terminal asks once when unset; agent-launched runs never block, the preflight says it is unset and the agent asks the operator; --keep-awake/--no-keep-awake per run; the Mac app toggles the same setting); (f) sync during a run (4.1) and presence (4.2) are PAID, following sofar-cloud v2-sync-team D2 (sync is the paid product): enforced by sofar-cloud's entitlement check on the server, never by licence code in the MIT engine; the engine's client code only acts for linked repos. payload.because: rust-core D1 moves status, statusline and hook handlers to Rust while `sofar drive` stays TypeScript, and the Mac app reads through the Rust core, so the lock's readers will be Rust and Swift. flock is the primitive both get with zero new dependencies, and Node can already take the same lock on macOS; the research is in note 01M2QX4KSFFX2QV68YG4QFSKA4.
payload.chose: 1.1(a): the run lock is an flock-semantics exclusive lock on a file keyed by run id. Rust takes it with std File::try_lock (flock on Unix, LockFileEx on Windows; no new crate under rust-core D1), Swift with flock, Node on macOS with fs.openSync(O_EXLOCK|O_NONBLOCK) (verified 2026-09-17 on Node 24.15 to contend with flock, held through SIGSTOP, released on kill -9). Node on Linux holds it through a flock(1) child tied to the driver until sofar-core binaries ship and take over; where flock(1) is absent the driver keeps today's refusal and says liveness cannot be checked. Windows follows sofar-core. Engines floor stays >=18. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").
payload.over: A listening unix socket (blocked by Claude Code's Linux seccomp and macOS Seatbelt sandboxes, stale socket files after kill -9, 104-byte path limit); node:sqlite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE (needs Node >=22.13 and a rusqlite crate on the Rust side, and SQLite's fcntl locks do not see flock on Linux); pid or hostname-pid files; heartbeat locks (proper-lockfile).
payload.rule: Take the run lock with flock semantics only — never fcntl/lockf, SQLite locks, sockets or pid files — so Node, Rust and Swift contend on the same lock.

payload.because: D2's reasons were that a pid is machine-local in a committed log and a reused pid signals a stranger. An empty file outside the repo carries nothing to commit and nothing to reuse: the kernel releases the lock when the holder dies, so no stale value can ever point at another process.
payload.chose: 1.1(b): QUALIFIES in-session-drive D2 (no pid in the record, no pid file beside it) without overturning it. An empty lock file under the per-user state dir ($XDG_STATE_HOME/sofar or ~/.local/state/sofar), whose liveness answer comes only from whether the OS reports the lock held, is not the pid file D2 forbids. D2's rule stands for pids. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").
payload.over: Reading D2 as forbidding any driver-owned file (leaving no way to tell a live driver from a dead one), or writing a pid into the lock file for diagnostics.
payload.rule: Never write a pid or any content into a run lock file, never place it under the repo, and never unlink it.

payload.because: Telemetry is data about the product's use sent to its maker; this ping is the operator's own run state delivered to the operator's own devices through sync they opted into, the same class as `sofar push`. The conditions make that distinction checkable rather than asserted.
payload.chose: 1.1(c): the driver's presence ping is user-facing sync, not telemetry emission — the CLAUDE.md guard-rail "DO NOT build … telemetry emission" is NAMED here and does not apply to it. Conditions that keep it sync: sent only for repos the operator linked to their own sofar cloud account, with an opt-out; payload is ids only; shown only to that repo's members; one server row per run, overwritten, deleted after the run; never used for product analytics; never written to events.jsonl. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").
payload.over: Treating the ping as telemetry and dropping remote presence (remote viewers could never tell a crashed driver from a running one), or folding presence into the record as periodic events.
payload.rule: Send driver presence only for cloud-linked repos, carrying ids only (run, initiative, task, state, seq, interval) — never content, never a record event, never analytics.

payload.because: Only the driver knows its own lifetime, and `caffeinate -w` ends by itself when the watched process exits, so no cleanup and no pid is stored anywhere. The operator asked for a way to be asked before a run and a setting to turn it on or off.
payload.chose: 1.1(e): keep-awake lives in the engine. On macOS the driver spawns `caffeinate -i -w <its own pid>` for the run's life. Setting `drive.keep_awake` (on/off) in ~/.config/sofar/config.json; a terminal run with the setting unset asks once and saves the answer; a detached or agent-launched run never prompts, and its preflight lines say the setting is unset so the agent asks the operator in chat; `--keep-awake` / `--no-keep-awake` override per run; the opening lines state that idle sleep is blocked but lid-close sleep is not. The paid Mac app may toggle the same setting. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").
payload.over: Keep-awake only in the paid Mac app (works only while the app runs, and cannot tie itself to the driver's lifetime); always on (surprising power use); a per-repo setting committed to git (sleep is a machine preference, not project state).
payload.rule: Never block a detached or agent-launched run on a keep-awake prompt; prompt only on a TTY, otherwise state the unset setting in the preflight lines.

payload.because: The engine is MIT (packages/engine/package.json), so a paywall in its code can be deleted by anyone; the server is the only place entitlement holds. Keeping the protection pieces free avoids charging users to prevent damage to their own repos.
payload.chose: 1.1(f): sync during a run (4.1) and driver presence (4.2) are paid features, following sofar-cloud v2-sync-team D2 ("sync IS the paid product"). sofar-cloud enforces entitlement on its push and presence endpoints; the MIT engine carries only the client code, acts only for linked repos, and on an entitlement refusal says so once and keeps the run going unsynced. Local pieces — run lock, fencing, --await, --follow, prompt line, statusline, keep-awake — touch no cloud and stay free. Paid pieces are designed for a 100-person repo first (sofar-cloud enterprise D1). Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").
payload.over: Shipping drive-time sync free in the engine, or gating it with licence code inside the engine.
payload.rule: Never add licence, plan or entitlement checks to the engine; paid features are enforced by sofar-cloud's server.

payload.text: 1.2 SPEC choices worth knowing before Phase 2: lock path is `<state base>/runs/<run id>.lock` (per user, not per clone); probes take a SHARED lock and read HELD/FREE/ABSENT, where ABSENT is `liveness unknown`, never `driver gone` (a GUI app with a different XDG env, another machine, or a pre-lock run). A claim retries 500ms. The refusal cannot name the live driver's log as plan task 2.1 says, because D3 forbids content in the lock file; it names `sofar drive --stop` and `sofar status` instead. Measured: Node's O_EXLOCK descriptor is close-on-exec, so a session still running after its driver's kill -9 leaves the lock free (lock = driver liveness, not session liveness). A fenced driver signals nothing, waits for its live session, files no handoff or stop, exits 1. Keep-awake setter is `sofar drive --keep-awake-setting <on|off>` (mirrors `sofar upgrade --auto`); the setting is re-read before each launch so an agent's mid-run answer applies from the next session. `--await` exit codes: 0 stopped, 2 driver gone, 1 nothing to await. Drive-time push is trailing 15s after growth plus at handoff and stop. rust-core parity impact noted in the rust-core record.

drive-visibility 2.1: run lock — one driver per run

A driver holds an empty flock-semantics lock at
<state base>/runs/<run id>.lock from before run_started until after
run_stopped; the kernel releases it on any death. macOS takes it with an
O_EXLOCK descriptor, Linux through a flock(1) child on a pipe from the
driver. A probe (shared, non-blocking) reads held / free / absent.

drive() refuses a fresh start and --resume while the run is held, says
"driver gone" and names --resume when the lock is free, and keeps the
record's own words when it is absent (liveness unknown, never gone).
Where no lock can be taken, the opening lines say liveness is
unavailable and the run proceeds. The state-base-inside-the-repo check
moves to state-dir.ts, shared with the diagnostics store.
EOF

payload.because: Ownership is the highest epoch, not the newest id, so the requests a driver must honour are those made after the adoption that put IT in force. Ids are ulids — they carry the time the timestamps did and every reader of the fold compares the same bytes. Changing the element rather than adding an array keeps one list; rust-core mirrors one line.
payload.chose: 2.2 fold shape: RunState gains `adoptions` [{id, ts, epoch}] and `owner` {id, epoch} (run_started's id at epoch 1 until an adoption outranks it), and `stop_requests` now carries event ids instead of envelope timestamps (name unchanged, every other reader used only its length). A stop request is in force when its id sorts after the OWNER's adoption — SPEC's "latest adoption" read as the adoption in force, and SPEC reworded to say so.
payload.over: Cutting at the latest adoption by id (a stale lower-epoch adoption synced in late would silence requests meant for the owner); a parallel `stop_request_ids` array beside the timestamps; keeping the wall-clock adoptedAt compare.

nothing. The one-time prompt ([Y/n], Enter means yes) is asked only when

payload.because: The line is what an agent's background shell hands back, so stdout carries only the outcome. The note is read once, at exit, so a decode there costs nothing per tick and changes nothing Rust mirrors. A tick stays a stat plus a lock probe, which is the "zero cost" the SPEC promises.
payload.chose: 3.1 --await shape: the outcome line goes to stdout (exit 0 stop, exit 2 driver gone); the ABSENT notice and the nothing-to-await refusal (exit 1) go to stderr. The line for a needs_user stop is describeRun plus "<task>'s note: <note>". The note comes from a decode of the log (decodeLines: replay order, corrections voided, same set/clear rule as the fold's blockNotes) at exit. The fold state is left as it was. The driver's byte scan becomes appendedBytesScan(path, from, markers), shared by watchRunEvents and --await.

export const DRIVE_LINE_BUDGET = 200

 * The drive line (drive-visibility 3.2): how the session's initiative's run

 * reason> · <n> handoffs · now on <task> · <done>/<total>` — for a run still
 * open or stopped since this session began, and ONLY when it moved since this
 * session last saw it. What counts as moving is the line itself minus the
 * liveness word: a handoff, a task finished, the task in flight, the stop. A
 * driver dying moves nothing in the record, so it shows here only beside

 * flock(1) spawn, and the per-prompt path spawns nothing unconditionally (D6).
 * A driven session (its agent launched with the driver's nudge path) gets no
 * line: it is the run, and every line there is paid by every session.

export function driveLine(
  rootDir: string,
  state: InitiativeState,
  me: SessionState,
  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,
  lock?: RunLockOptions,
): string | null {

  const run = latestRun(state)

  const n = run.handoffs.length

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""drive-visibility 3.5 probe: host an INTERACTIVE Claude Code session in a
pty, type one prompt, then leave it idle for `seconds`, draining its output."""
import os, pty, select, sys, time
cwd, prompt, seconds, log = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], float(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4]
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.chdir(cwd)
    os.environ['TERM'] = 'xterm-256color'
    os.environ.pop('CLAUDECODE', None)
    os.execvp('claude', ['claude', '--model', 'haiku'])
out = open(log, 'ab', buffering=0)
def pump(t):
    end = time.time() + t
    buf = b''
    while time.time() < end:
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.5)
        if fd in r:
            try: data = os.read(fd, 65536)
            except OSError: return buf
            out.write(data); buf += data
    return buf
seen = pump(8)
if b'trust' in seen.lower():
    os.write(fd, b'\r'); pump(6)
os.write(fd, prompt.encode()); pump(1); os.write(fd, b'\r')
out.write(f'\n[host] prompt sent {time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")}\n'.encode())
pump(seconds)
out.write(f'\n[host] exiting {time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")}\n'.encode())
os.write(fd, b'/exit\r'); pump(5)
try: os.kill(pid, 9)
except ProcessLookupError: pass
EOF

- DETACH FROM INSIDE A SESSION: an interactive Claude Code session (2.1.280, haiku) wrote back with `sofar event append … session_ended`, then ran `sofar drive proof --detach --model haiku --keep-awake --session-timeout 600`. Driver pid 92142 at 19:36:33Z; the opening lines carried the run id, the keep-awake line and the stop command.
- WHILE RUNNING (19:36:56Z): status `running`; prompt line `sofar drive: run … running · 0 handoffs · now on 1.1 · 0/2`; statusline `proof 0/2 · drive 1.1`; `pmset -g assertions` showed caffeinate asserting on behalf of Process ID 92142.
- SECOND DRIVER REFUSED: `sofar drive proof --resume` → "is being driven right now — a driver on this machine holds its run lock", naming `sofar status` and `--stop`. Nothing appended.
- KILL -9 (exact PID) at 19:37:10.711Z: the hook's `--await` exited 2 at 19:37:11 (≤0.3 s) with the driver-gone line; status read `driver gone — no stop recorded and the run lock on this machine is free; --resume picks it up`; statusline `drive gone` (red); the caffeinate assertion was gone, proving keep-awake lasts exactly the driver's life. The PROMPT LINE stayed silent, as designed: liveness is not part of its fingerprint, so a death shows there only beside news.
- WAKE: the idle calling session was woken at 19:37:14.4Z — 3.7 s after the kill — by the asyncRewake PostToolUse hook (timeout 21600), and answered with the line unprompted. The needs_user wake itself was proven in 3.5 probe A; live here the needs_user stop was caught by `--await` in a shell instead (exit 0).
- RESUME AND FENCE at 19:37:51Z: `--resume --detach` printed "resuming run … 0 handoff(s) already recorded" and "adopted at epoch 2 — a driver still holding an earlier epoch steps down when it sees this". Driver pid 92777.
- RUN COMPLETED ~19:40:48Z: 3 handoffs (1 stall, 1 task_done, 1 needs_user); `stopped: needs_user — 1.2 is blocked — read its note`; `--await` exited 0 quoting the driven session's own question: "Which colour should be used for task 1.2? Please choose one: blue or red". alpha.txt contained exactly `alpha` (1.1 really done by a driven session). Post-stop: prompt line `stopped: needs_user · 3 handoffs · 1/2`; statusline `proof 1/2 · drive needs_user` (yellow); the driver exited with the run.
- ENDING THE CALLING SESSION DOES NOT KILL A DETACHED DRIVER: a third run (01M35A6EHDH3ZE2DYN7JS8A6ZJ) was detached from a fresh calling session using the test stub binary (no model calls). Its driver (94499) already had PPID 1 and its own process group; killing the calling Claude Code process left the driver ALIVE and the run `running`, and `sofar drive proof --stop` then ended it cleanly ("stopped: interrupted — stop requested with `sofar drive --stop`").
Cost: 6 short haiku sessions in total (3 driven, 3 calling, one of those wasted on a dialog mishap). The adapter reported no cost figure for this run, so no dollar total is claimed.

Two incidents from the 5.1 proof, both worth keeping:
(1) PRODUCT FINDING — a calling session's SessionStart registration did not land in a freshly-trusted repo. The session (ad59aa44) ran, wrote back through the CLI dialect, and detached a run, but its `session_ended` folded with `warning: session "ad59aa44…" ended without session_started — stub created`, so the fold carries a stub session for it. The likely cause is that Claude Code does not run project hooks until the folder's trust dialog is answered, so the SessionStart shim never fired for the first session in a newly trusted repo; every later session in that repo registers normally. Consequence: `sofar drive --detach`'s refusal gate ("the calling session is registered and has not written back") cannot see an unregistered caller, so it lets the detach through — in this proof the caller HAD written back, but the gate was not what proved it. Same family as the torn-session finding carried to record-integrity: a session's identity is not settled at the moment its first events are written.
(2) HARNESS NOTE for anyone driving a Claude Code session from a pty: TWO dialogs can stand between launch and the prompt — the trust check (which defaults to "No, exit" when the folder pre-approves tools, so send Down before Enter) and the .mcp.json server approval (whose default "Continue without using this MCP server" is right for a CLI-dialect caller). An unanswered dialog silently eats whatever is typed next: the first attempt's prompt went into the MCP dialog and the session sat idle for seven minutes. The host in scratchpad proof51/host51.py answers both.

payload.text:
Follow-up on the trust-dialog finding (sofar-c3's framing, 2026-09-22): the fault is not that registration fails, it is that it fails QUIETLY, and the condition is DETECTABLE. `sofar drive --detach`'s gate looks for the calling session's registration to decide whether it owes a write-back; when it finds none it proceeds silently, which reads identically to "this caller is not registered on this initiative, all good". It should say what it found instead — one line naming that no registration exists for this session id, so an operator in a freshly-trusted repo learns their hooks have not run yet rather than discovering it later in the fold's `ended without session_started` warning. Cheap, and it turns a silent state into a stated one. Not scheduled here; it belongs with 3.7 or with whatever picks up the record-integrity successor.
Worth recording as the shape of the night, across every lane: each significant finding was a SILENT failure — hooks dying at their timeout without a word (3.5 probes B and E); the trust dialog withholding registration without a word (5.1); and, in the other lanes sofar-c3 is carrying, a re-run inheriting a discarded attempt's memory, a cell sandbox manufacturing a memory win, and a spend cap blind outside a cells root. None announced itself; every one was caught by someone checking. That is the argument for sofar's own principle of loud failure, and tonight is its evidence.

BLAST RADIUS of the silent 600 s hook timeout: the NEW feature only — no hook sofar ships today can approach it. The four read-path hooks are file reads plus a bounded fold, measured end to end tonight (node spawn included) at session-start 98 ms, user-prompt 62 ms, stop 63 ms, statusline 63 ms p50 on the repo fixture; on the 1,000-initiative / 10 MB i1000-10mb fixture the same bench holds a ±10% gate where a 30–36 ms move counts as a large regression. Tens to hundreds of milliseconds against 600 s.
ONE CAVEAT, and it is a silent coupling of the same shape as tonight's findings: the Stop hook is not purely a fold — it runs the operator's own executable decision checks (memory-lead 2.3), capped at STOP_CHECK_MAX_MS 30 s per check and STOP_CHECK_BUDGET_MS 45 s total. Today that sits 13× under the default. The day someone raises those caps for a good local reason, the Stop hook starts dying silently at ten minutes and the change that caused it will look unrelated: no error, no log line, just write-backs that stop happening. The two constants live in different files and nothing connects them.
SO 3.7 SHIPS THE COUPLING AS A TEST, not a comment: one assertion that STOP_CHECK_BUDGET_MS plus fold headroom stays under the hook timeout sofar configures, so a future cap raise fails the build in front of whoever raises it. A comment at the constant is a fine second line; the test is the one that does the work. Smallest instance of the loud-failure principle the whole night argues for, which is why it belongs in this task.

payload.text: A vitest file that fails to LOAD is reported as "not run", never as a failure, so a suite can say PASSED while covering less than it claims — compare test COUNTS, not the word "passed", whenever the environment differs from the one the baseline ran in. Caught staging 0.34.0-rc.1: the release branch reported 3008 passed / 16 skipped against an independent verification of the main it merged at 3011 / 16. The missing three were packages/schema/test/rust-codegen.test.ts, whose top-level import of tools/schema-codegen/emit.mjs needs the devDependency ts-json-schema-generator; the file's own `it.skipIf(cargo missing)` cannot protect an import that never resolved. The cause was a worktree symlinking the main checkout's node_modules (see M6) where that dep is not installed. Fix: give a release worktree its own `npm ci`, then re-run and confirm the count matches or exceeds the base's. A release gated on a suite that quietly skipped a file is not gated.

5.2 gate re-run and install proof, after sofar-c3 caught a three-test gap (2026-09-23):
- THE GAP WAS REAL AND IS CLOSED. The first gate run reported 3008 passed / 16 skipped against 3011 / 16 for the independent verification of main at 23243e8. packages/schema/test/rust-codegen.test.ts holds exactly three tests and failed to LOAD (its top-level import needs the devDependency ts-json-schema-generator, absent from the shared node_modules the worktree was symlinking). A load failure reports as "not run", so the suite still said PASSED while covering three tests less — tonight's silent-failure shape once more, in my own gate. Re-ran with the worktree's own `npm ci`: 3011 passed, 16 skipped, NO failures, matching the base exactly. The earlier "pre-existing failure on main" framing was true but beside the point: what mattered was that my gate had not run the file at all.
- INSTALL FALLBACK IS NOW PROVEN, not assumed. No published version has ever carried the five sofar-core-<platform> optional dependencies (0.32.0 publishes none; rc.2 was never published), so "npm skips a 404 optional dep" had no evidence behind it. Installed THIS tarball into an empty scratch prefix: npm skipped all five 404s, exit 0, zero sofar-core packages present, the JavaScript shim left in place, and the installed bin reported 0.34.0-rc.1. So the operator can publish without a separate post-publish smoke, though one costs nothing.
- The annotated tag v0.34.0-rc.1 was re-cut at the same commit (bd0a898) so its notes carry the corrected count and the install proof. Deleting and recreating an UNPUSHED tag rewrites nothing anyone has seen; shipping a tag whose notes state a wrong test count would have been the worse outcome.

payload.text: Release tags: an UNPUSHED tag may be deleted and re-cut — nobody has seen it, so that is editing a draft, and shipping notes known to be wrong is the real damage. The moment a tag is PUSHED it becomes something others have seen, and any correction after that is a NEW tag, never a move: no `git tag -f`, no delete-and-repush. The rule is not "never move a tag", it is "never rewrite what someone else has seen". A corrective tag name like v0.34.0-rc.1a is the wrong answer BEFORE a push (it permanently advertises a mistake that never left the worktree) and the only answer after one. Set staging 0.34.0-rc.1 (drive-visibility 5.2), where the first tag's notes carried a test count that a re-run corrected.

Two things for the operator's morning, from staging 0.34.0-rc.1:
(1) THE REGISTRY STATE IS NOT "0.33 then 0.34". 0.33 never shipped in any form: rc.2 was never published (it exists only as a git tag and a local ~/.bench build), and the published 0.32.0 carries no optionalDependencies at all. So npm's `latest` is 0.32.0, and after publishing this rc the picture is latest=0.32.0, next=0.34.0-rc.1, and nothing in between. That is still coherent — `next` is exactly for this, and 0.33.0 stable lands on `latest` after round 2 — but the interim state is worth knowing before someone reads `next` as "one ahead of latest".
(2) STILL DO THE POST-PUBLISH SMOKE, even though the fallback is proven: install from the REGISTRY into a scratch dir (`npm install sofar.sh@next`) and run `sofar --version`. The proof I ran tested the tarball path; the registry path is a different one even if it should behave identically, and it costs one command.
Tag rule boundary, recorded as M8 because the precedent matters: re-cutting v0.34.0-rc.1 was right only because it was UNPUSHED. Once pushed, a correction is a NEW tag, never a move.

plan.goal: An operator always knows whether a drive run is alive and how far it has got — in the calling session, on the status bar, and in the sofar apps — without asking an agent or opening another terminal, and one run can never be driven by two drivers at once. Liveness is decided by a machine-local lock the OS releases on exit, never by a heartbeat or a record event; a heartbeat exists only to show presence to remote viewers.

tasks.title: Operator rulings, each logged as a Decision before dependent work. Recommended in the 2026-09-17 session: (a) lock primitive = flock semantics everywhere — Rust std File::try_lock (zero crates under rust-core D1), Swift flock, Node O_EXLOCK on macOS (verified to contend with flock), Linux flock(1) child until sofar-core binaries ship; no Node floor raise, no node:sqlite/rusqlite; (b) an empty OS-released lock file under the per-user state dir is NOT the pid file in-session-drive D2 forbids (clarify D2, do not overturn); (c) the presence ping is user-facing sync for cloud-linked repos, not telemetry emission; (e) keep-awake lives in the engine as a ~/.config/sofar setting (terminal asks once when unset; agent-launched runs never block, the preflight says it is unset and the agent asks the operator; --keep-awake/--no-keep-awake per run; the Mac app toggles the same setting); (f) sync during a run (4.1) and presence (4.2) are PAID, following sofar-cloud v2-sync-team D2 (sync is the paid product): enforced by sofar-cloud's entitlement check on the server, never by licence code in the MIT engine; the engine's client code only acts for linked repos.
